deferred_human_review_runtime: Library issue for @941design/nostr-events maintainers: the simple-pool transport de-duplicates by event id BEFORE signature verification, so a relay sending a forged event that reuses a genuine event id first gets the forgery rejected AND the genuine event dropped as a duplicate (message-suppression by a hostile relay). Found by app/tests/unit/marmot/client/transport.forgery.harness.test.ts. Not fixable in-app without a custom verifier (AC-TRANS-1 forbids one).

Pre-existing gap (not caused by this epic): call signaling signs inner kinds 25050-25055 with the account signer, but neither the old nor the new NIP-46 permission set requests them — calls may fail under permission-enforcing bunkers. AC-SIGN-3 fixes the app-added set to exactly {0,20602,30078,10050}; adding call kinds needs a spec change.

S3 accepted residual: if the account is torn down (sign-out/signer change) while a withdrawn message dispatch is still running past its 10 s bound, its late retract is dropped and the withdrawn message stays in the chat store. Requires a fork-withdraw + >10 s handler + teardown in the same window.

S5 decider (recompute-on-retract): after a fork rewind, edits/deletes/reactions/poll results are rebuilt from retained group history — a withdrawn delete or edit makes earlier content visible again, admin-gated deletes are re-judged against the CURRENT admin list, and the original text of an edited/deleted message stays on the device (in the history store and the slot base snapshot) until the group is left.

S5 accepted residual: votes are keyed by poll id, so if a poll open is withdrawn while ANOTHER member open for the same poll id remains (requires deliberate id reuse), earlier votes count toward the surviving poll. Live dispatch behaves the same.
